title: 13th Sitting of First session of 2026
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 on Tuesday 28 April 2026 (minutes no. 2026/1/13). Most of this part was question time with Dr. Abdulla Mutthalib, Minister of Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development, where about two dozen MPs asked about paused flat agreements, island housing units, harbours, roads, water and sewerage, and housing loans. The minister declined several questions as unrelated to housing. The chair ruled that an urgent matter on a police search of a newspaper office did not meet the Rules of Procedure, and debate then began on a bill to amend the Constitution to bring back atoll councils; the text ends partway through that debate. This part continues the debate on a constitutional amendment, proposed by the North Galolhu member for the MDP, that would restore the pre-amendment rules on atoll councils (Articles 230 and 231). MDP members argued that abolishing atoll councils removed help and coordination for islands and added new layers of government, and urged a return to the earlier text. PNC members said atoll councils delivered little, that the amendment was unnecessary, and that the debate was wasting floor time; some exchanges drifted into the President's press conference and press freedom, which the chair twice steered back to the amendment. No vote was taken, and the sitting closed with the next one set for 29 April 2026 at 9:00 am. The text starts mid-speech and is partly garbled.

speakers.name: Dr. Abdulla Mutthalib
positions: Said flat agreement signing was paused after unfairness in the gazetted allocation list was noticed, to protect those entitled; he called it not political.
Said Thilamale Bridge works continue with the contractor given more time, and it could be usable by 2027.
Said Rasmale is needed as Greater Male has little land left; loan-financed and Bank of Maldives units continue across islands.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked why flat allocations and agreement signing changed suddenly, and for a status update and completion date for Thilamale Bridge.
Asked how the 2025 housing budget was spent and when the Kunahandhoo and Fenfushi water and sewerage works would finish.
As bill sponsor, argued abolishing atoll councils lacked study and public approval and that the Constitution assumes full decentralisation.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked for completion dates for Thoddoo roads, Rasdhoo harbour and flats, and Ukulhas coastal protection works.
Asked what price Bank of Maldives paid for HDC land and what payment help flat residents on islands will get.
Asked when work on the planned 50 housing units in Ukulhas would begin and residents could move in.
Supported the amendment; said abolishing atoll councils slowed island services and development, and that reversing the changes would restore island-level service delivery.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked whether the therapy-documentation rule is fair for people with special needs who do not require therapy.
Asked whether island flats will have special arrangements for people needing special assistance, and about 700 flats under a previous government.
Asked when work on the planned housing units in Vaikaradhoo, Kurinbi and Nethlaidhoo would begin.
Supported the amendment; said the abolition of atoll councils ended much assistance to islands and that problems should be fixed by reverting to the earlier constitution text.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Said the 5 percent housing loan is hard to access because of Bank of Maldives and MMA rules, and raised Nilandhoo sewerage delays.
Asked whether the contractor on a stalled sewerage project could be dropped and the work reassigned.
Opposed the amendment, saying it was not a real or sensible change, would waste the floor's time, and that decentralisation had already given councils more power.
Raised a point of order that talk of the President's press conference was off the bill; the chair said it had already told the member to stay on topic.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when the stalled Noomaraa harbour project would restart and when the Kanditheemu harbour work would be completed.
Asked when the enlarged home-building loan would reach youth who qualify but have not yet received it.
Supported the amendment; said atoll councils had delivered services and funds to islands and that reverting all the constitutional changes would also cut layers of administration.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked when plot holders in Gulhifalhu, Giraavaru Falhu and Hulhumale Phase 3 can settle, and why Rasmale is being prioritised.
Supported the amendment; said abolishing atoll councils saves no money and swaps elected bodies for appointees; also criticised the President's press conference and called for press freedom.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked whether patients with long-term illness in the atolls are prioritised for flats, and what is done about social housing being rented out.
Asked how much state budget would be spent reclaiming plots given in Gulhifalhu, Giraavaru Falhu and Hulhumale Phase 3.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked for details on why the Hithadhoo harbour works begun by MTCC are badly delayed; the chair reminded him to respect the Rules of Procedure.
Said his August 2025 question went unanswered and asked how many housing projects have moved beyond foundation stones.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when land reclamation around his constituency would start and when the Kelaa housing project would begin.
Asked whether spending on reclaiming land given out from the sea was justified against the number of homes it could provide.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Asked for a date when Holhudhoo's water supply works would be completed, noting residents' concerns and a petition.
Opposed the amendment; drawing on his time as an island clerk, said atoll councils achieved little and called for the amendment to be put to a vote and set aside.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked when flats started under this government would be finished and residents moved in.
Opposed the amendment; said atoll councils added a costly layer with little benefit to his area, and spoke at length on rights and independent institutions.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Asked what rights holders of flats given by earlier governments now have, and how those lists were changed.
In the debate, argued the amendment was unnecessary, saying island and city councils already serve residents, and criticised opposition leaders.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked for an update on Kunahandhoo, where people are living with contaminated water.
Said his constituency has no housing unit and no sewerage; the minister said he would call him.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Asked whether new plots and flats will be allocated the same way as before, and when the 50-unit Kudahuvadhoo project can proceed.
Asked when the Dh. Vaani housing issue would be resolved and whether agreements can be cancelled outside court.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked when the Keyodhoo reclamation promised to finish by April 2026 would be done.
Asked whether people relocated from islands get any priority for Male flats and plots.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Opposed the amendment; said atoll councils had been shrunk by law already, the amendment was not worth the floor time, and recalled MDP's 2008 reform promises.
Raised a point of order saying the Vaikaradhoo member's remarks about him were false; the chair ruled it was not a point of order.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked when the 100 housing units built in Thulhaadhoo about three years ago would be handed over, saying they have deteriorated.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked about untarred Velidhoo roads after seven years, Foddhoo harbour materials, and when stalled sewerage work would restart.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Asked when practical work on the planned 100 HDC housing units in Hithadhoo would start, and when Hithadhoo-Addu link road work begins.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Abdul Rahman
positions: Asked when water and sewerage works begun under the previous government would be finished and when airport work would resume.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rasheed
positions: Asked about unsafe buildings in Male and whether a stalled Omadhoo water system contract could be cancelled and reassigned.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked how far work on the planned Fiyoori housing units has progressed.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked how far design has progressed for the planned 2,000-unit Kulhudhuffushi project and when work will begin.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked for easier paperwork than proof of 15 years living in Male when applying for housing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Asked about the gazetted 500-unit Thulusdhoo housing project and its status.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Supported the amendment; argued atoll councils are needed to plan regional services and use island resources, and urged the President to revert his constitutional changes.

decisions: Hassan Waheed (Vilifushi) was named to the Committee on Government Accountability in place of Ali Ibrahim (West Henveyru), effective 27 April 2026.
The chair announced committee reporting deadlines: 31 July 2026 for aviation and land transport bills and 31 August 2026 for the Thalassemia Control Act amendment.
The chair said Meekail Ahmed Nasym's urgent matter on police entering a newspaper office did not meet Rule 197 conditions, so it could not be taken up as an urgent matter.
Debate on the atoll councils constitutional amendment continued; no vote was taken in this part.
The Majlis took a 30-minute recess and resumed with the Speaker in the chair.
Next sitting announced for Wednesday 29 April 2026 at 9:00 am.
